newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Jalisco state to promote mining.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Jalisco state to promote mining.

text.p: The western Mexican state of Jalisco next year will launch a program aimed at promoting mining, a state spokesman said Monday.
Bernardo Brito Miranda, spokesman for the economic promotion ministry of Jalisco state, said the program would be developed by the end of October and launched on January 1.
The so-called Half Moon of Gold and Silver program will seek to promote mining in the areas of metals, non-metals and semi-precious stones.
"There are a lot of companies with concessions and land to mine, the problem is that they don't have the economic capacity to develop projects," Brito said.

Among the measures Jalisco plans to promote mining are incorporating the mining sector into the State Deregulation Commission and boosting state-backed financing to small and medium-sized mining companies, Brito said.
He said the second Jalisco Mining Forum, scheduled for October 24-25, would attempt to attract foreign and national mining capital to the state.
Brito said a total of 40 companies would be mining in Jalisco next year.
